cards.note: Tiranë has a big mountain range in the east, combined with gen 3 and double blue stripes on the license plates, 100% Tiranë.
Graz street signs are green with white text.
Innsbruck street signs are very dark red/brown with white text.

Poles in Vienna and Innsbruck feature these red-and-white pieces of tape that look like the Austrian flag. They can be differentiated by the fact that the tapes in Vienna are thinner, and there are typically two on each pole.

Linz has these 2 different street signs, a black street sign with white text, and a unique street sign thats white with black text and has orange stripes above and under and an orange logo on the left.
Salzburg street sign.
Vienna street sign.

Poles in Vienna and Innsbruck feature these red-and-white pieces of tape that look like the Austrian flag. They can be differentiated by the fact that the tapes in Vienna are thinner, and there are typically two on each pole.
Antwerp street signs have the name Antwerpen written on them.
Brussels street signs have dutch and french written on them aswell as the city names on the top with a logo.
Ghent street signs have the name Gent written on them.
These 2 street signs can be found in Plovdiv, the left one is more common.

White street signs with two red strips; one covering the bottom and one covering part of the top, can be found in Sofia.

NOTE: You can also find other types of street signs in Sofia.
Brown street signs with bright yellow text can be found in Stara Zagora.

Split, the 2nd biggest city in Croatia, is a distinct city surrounded by water, with big mountain ridges to the north and east. It has lots of big apartment buildings and 1 sky scraper which can sometimes be seen. An island can also sometimes be seen towards the west.
These 2 dark blue street signs are unique to Zagreb. It always has a white line next to the street name.

Pairs of black and white house numbers are found in Brno.

NOTE: The city district can be found written on the black house number.
České Budějovice street signd are red and have the city name written on the bottom.
Plzeň house numbers typically consist of two red and white octagonal plates with inverse colour schemes.
Prague street signs are very unique, they're red with a very unique and fancy looking frame around it. Their also big.
Aarhus has white street signs with blue text.

Within Denmark, Copenhagen has black street signs with white text.

NOTE: The centre of Odense also has black street signs with white text, but has a white frame added within it.

Odense street signs are attached to a metal pole that has a 90° angle in it, be aware that these street sign poles can be found rarely in other towns on the island of Funen. But Odense has these spammed in every corner useally.
Tallinn street signs are blue with white text, often with a white with blue house number next to it.
Tartu street signs are black with white text and a white frame in it + the corners have dots.
Helsinki street signs have 2 street signs on top of each other, they often have a unique font aswell.

Helsinki features these unique green-and-yellow trams.

NOTE: Tampere is the only other Finnish city with trams, but they are red instead of green and yellow.
Buses in Turku are uniquely yellow, with a white rear.
Small tables with “Arrᵗ” written on a small separate sign, are found in Bordeaux, despite being a city not divided into arrondissements.
Street signs with a red slanted fleur-de-lis are unique to Lille.

Lyon’s street signs feature four corner bolts and an uninterrupted inner white border that cuts a notch for the arrondissement and each bolt.

NOTE: Outside Lyon proper, the street sign will display the name of the suburb instead.
Marseille’s street signs will usually feature the city’s emblem, a variation of the Greek cross. The white border will usually be interrupted at the top, even when the cross is absent.
Montpellier street signs will typically contain a blue ‘M’ on a white background in the top left corner.

cards.a: France - Nantes and Rennes street sign
cards.note: Nantes and Rennes have this street sign with the special corners and the dots in them. But Nantes is alot bigger so guessing Nantes would be the better option, unless you know its Rennes.

Paris uses an iconic green & Prussian blue design with a top arch that has also been replicated in Bucharest, which is sometimes referred to as Paris of the east.

NOTE: The simple rectangular form of the sign can be found in the towns nearby and rarely in other cities.
Toulouse has these unique street signs.
Berlin uses bright orange bins that have white text on them.
Berlin uses white signs with a grey border, and a separate section for numbers under the street name. Also note how the letter ß looks.

Lampposts in Cologne will often feature these bright yellow numbers on a black piece of plastic.

NOTE: Similar looking things can be found elsewhere as well.
Dortmund uses blue signs with a white border and a grey frame. The signs also have a separate section for numbers under the street name.
Dresden has blue signs with a unique font.
Düsseldorf has black signs with a white border, similar to Munich. The signs have a metallic frame.
Essen has blue signs with a very thick metallic frame.
Frankfurt uses blue street signs with a metallic border around the sign, as well as the separate section for numbers under the street name.
Hamburg uses bright red bins, with white speech bubbles.
Leipzig street signs are blue with a white frame in it with fancy corners.
Munich has blue street signs with a white decorative border that does not touch the corners. Also note the unique font.
Nuremberg has blue signs with a unique font. The signs also have a metal frame with a small gap between it and the sign.
Stuttgart uses black signs without a border.
Athens has this street sign with an extra part under the main street sign.
Yellow taxis with a blue stripe around the taxi are found in Athens.
In Thessaloniki, you will often see a large amount of unusually tall antennas on top of buildings.
Blue taxis with a white roof are found in Thessaloniki.
Budapest street signs have a district number in roman numerals followed by ''Kerület''.
Győr has large diagional corners.
Kecskemét has blue text with angular corners.
This street sign is found everywhere in Iceland but Reykjavik is the only big city in Iceland, its an easy city to recognize within Iceland.
Cork is relatively unique in that it is significantly more hilly than the other big Irish cities.

Dublin has blue street signs with white text and a white border around it, it also has a number on the right, showing in which district your in. Here is a map of postal areas in Dublin for guessing within the city.
Bari street signs have this unique logo in the top left.
Bologna street signs are white with blue text and a blue edge, the sign is sometimes supported by 3 small supports (1 on top, 2 on bottom).
Florence street signs are supported by 3 small supports (1 on top, 2 on bottom).
Milan street signs have a number in the top left.
Naples street signs have a unique font with an extra name under the street name.
Palermo has big mountains in the south and west.
Palermo street signs have 4 dots in each corner.
Rome street signs are by far the most distinct street signs in Italy, their bigger than any other street sign in Italy, they have a very thick frame and the Roman numerals in the top right.
Turin street signs have this unique font, sometimes they also have the date of the years on the bottom.
Venice can typically be recognized by its many canals running through most of the city.
Riga street signs are dark blue or black with white text and a white frame and commonly end with iela.
Riga buses and trams are white with a blue bottom, VERY similar to the dutch ones.
Kaunas house numbers are very big, with curvy lines above and under the numbers.
Vilnius street signs are white with black text and a black frame in it. The house number has the same design and is often next to the street name.
Luxembourg City has these unique street signs, the corners have blue triangle shapes.
Amsterdam street signs feature the city district in a smaller font size below the actual street name.

If you know your in The Netherlands, and you see many tall buildings, you will most likely be in Rotterdam. This city has the majority of skyscrapers within The Netherlands.

NOTE: The Hague and Amsterdam also have some tall buildings but not as much as Rotterdam.
Skopje has mountains in the north and south, the north mountain is even bigger and you can often see a cross on top of it.
You can find this specific design of green fire hydrants in Bergen.
Fairly large black or red pole plates can be found in Oslo.
Two red stripes going around lamp posts are commonly found in Stavanger.
Białystok uses turquoise street signs, with the district marked on the bottom.
Bydgoszcz street signs have a white frame in the sign with white dots in the corners.
Częstochowa street signs are blue with a yellow intersection on the bottom.
Gdańsk street signs have a brown intersection on the bottom.
Katowice street signs are black with yellow on the bottom, the city name is written in the yellow.
Kraków street signs are white with blue text and frame.
Lublin street signs are blue with a metal border around it, between the sign and the border is space.
Street signs in Poznań are mainly black, with the district being marked on the blue section at the bottom.
Szczecin uses colourful green and blue signs. The city district is marked on the bottom.
Warsaw and Łódź street signs are either blue or brown, majority being blue, with a red part on the bottom that has the city district written on it.
Wrocław street signs are either blue or brown, majority being blue, with a red part on the bottom that has the city district written on it, under the red part there is also a thick yellow stripe.
Lisbon street signs have 4 big screws in each corner.
Lime green street signs can be found in Porto.
Brașov has a lush green mountain with 2 towers on top and has Brașov written on the right in white letters.

Bucharest has 2 different street signs, the most common one is the one on the bottom, its literally the same as the paris version but language will obviously tell the difference. The other one has the same colors and uses white arrows.
Buzău street signs have an orange/blue B on the left, it also says the city name under it.
Cluj-Napoca uses white and pink buses and white, pink and gray trams. The city name can be seen on the side of the buses.
Constanța street signs have this unique orange shield logo on the left and above it is the city name written.
Timișoara taxis are white, which is not unique to Timișoara, but the purple sticker on the side is. It has municipiul Timișoara taxi written on the top of it.
Kazan has this extremely unique street sign.

Moscow street signs are blue with white text, their bigger than any other russian city street sign and are commonly spread throughout the city. The house numbers are also as big and sometimes the street signs can have different shapes.

St. Petersburg street signs include a transliteration of the street name on a black background with a unique logo on top with fancy borders. There is always another sign under it with a number written on in. They are primarily found downtown.
Belgrade street signs have cyrillic and latin written on them, it also has a unique shield icon on the left which has the serbian flag colors in it.
Bratislava buses and trams are red.
Košice has blue, yellow and white buses and trams.
Trolleybuses in Žilina use a green-yellow-white colour scheme. The trolley supporting electricity poles, often doubling as lamps, are painted with matching yellow and green colours.
Ljubljana street signs are green with a white fancy frame in it, the house numbers in Ljubljana are also green.
Taxis in Barcelona are black with yellow doors, including the trunk door.
The city of Bilbao uses this unique street sign, with a very elaborately decorated frame.

Madrid has 2 different kinds of street signs, the bottom one, found in the centre, is a very unique street sign, every street sign has a different picture shown. The street sign above is found outside of its centre, its blue with white text, but has a very important logo on the left, looks like a crown on top of something. There are a few slightly different versions of this crown logo throughout this city. So make sure to look if there is a crown on top of the logo.
Murcia street signs are blue with this thick white edge and have this unique logo on the left with a crown.
Seville street signs are pretty unique, each individual name has its own section with this unique font.
Velencia street signs have this unique logo on the top left.
Zaragoza street signs are white with a unique logo in the top left and also has a fancy decorated blue frame, they kinda look like many leaves.

The entire city of Gothenburg uses these unique blue street signs. Note that they almost always have two lines.

NOTE: Some other cities will have blue street signs near the centre, however they use a different design.
These somewhat old-looking, white street signs, with black corners, can be found all throughout Malmö.

Street signs in Stockholm will have two rows divided by a black line and will usually lack a black border. Similar signs can also rarely be found in central Gävle.

NOTE: Several suburbs in Stockholm use plain white street signs.
Large blue street signs, attached to a low double signpost, similar to directional signs in Denmark, are found in Basel.

If you know your in Switzerland and you see these dark blue street signs with Rue written on it, The only city that has these is Geneva.

NOTE: This design can commonly be found in France so make sure to confirm your in switzerland.
Zurich street signs are blue with a white edge and 4 thick dots in each corner.

Street signs in the Ankara Province are blue with a small round top. Similar street signs can very rarely be found in Giresun.

Beware that some newer street signs are red.
Antalya has a huge mountain range in the west, sometimes snow can be seen on top of it.
Antalya street signs are very simillar to the istanbul version, except that the Antalya version has a rounded logo in the bottom left.

Street signs in Bursa are green, and generally have slightly extruded letters, meaning the signs are not completely flat.

NOTE: Several other types of infrastructure in Bursa, such as fences and guardrails, may also be coloured green.

Eskişehir has 2 street signs, both blue, but the one on top has 2 white lines on the top and bottom. The bottom one has 3 intersections with text in each one. The street sign on the top is more common.
Gaziantep street signs are blue and oval shaped with a white edge inside it.

Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both Istanbul and in other cities. However, if you see such signs in combination with red house numbers, then you should be in Istanbul.
Street signs in the Izmir Province are dark blue, noticeably bulge outwards and very commonly have the emblem of Izmir in white at the top of the sign.

Donetsk and Odesa are the only 2 cities that only have 2011 coverage, all the coverage within those cities is taken in the autumn, which means you will see many orange and yellow leaves on the trees. Donetsk has long antenna, Odesa has short antenna.

NOTE: Kyiv, Lviv and Kharkiv also have autumn coverage but the majority has been overwritten by the newer summer coverage so you will rarely see those cities in autumn aswell.
Kharkiv street signs are blue with a white line in the middle, top text is written in cyrillic and the bottom is written in latin. The house numbers also have the same design.
These poles, with a red band across them, are unique to Kryvyi Rih.
If you know your in Ukraine, and you see many large and tall buildings, your most likely in Kyiv.

cards.a: Ukraine - Lviv streets and street sign
cards.note: Lviv streets have unique cobblestone pavement which really isnt found anywhere else in Ukraine except some smaller cities in the far west. It also has a unique street sign with a castel logo on the left which you can use to confirm Lviv.

Donetsk and Odesa are the only 2 cities that only have 2011 coverage, all the coverage within those cities is taken in the autumn, which means you will see many orange and yellow leaves on the trees. Donetsk has long antenna, Odesa has short antenna.

NOTE: Kyiv, Lviv and Kharkiv also have autumn coverage but the majority has been overwritten by the newer summer coverage so you will rarely see those cities in autumn aswell.
Aberdeen is a very easy recognizable city, 99% of all buildings are made out of grey sandstone.

Depending where you are in Belfast, you can often see these mountains with lots of trees on it (gets more bald on the top) to the west/north-west, sometimes with 1 or 2 towers on top of it. Hills can also be seen in the east/south east.

If your not sure these mountains are the Belfast mountains, check for clues to confirm your in Northern Ireland and it will 100% be Belfast.
The majority of poles and signposts in Birmingham have either yellow tape or yellow paint wrapped around them. Lampposts will also usually have this yellow sticker.
Street signs in Bristol will always have ''BS'' with a number written on the right side. This one is easy to remember because BS stands for Bri-Stol.

Edinburgh buildings are mostly made out of yellow/brown sandstone.

NOTE: Glasgow also has yellow/brown sandstone but also has red sandstone buildings.

cards.a: United Kingdom - Glasgow pink sticker + architecture
cards.note: This pink sticker with the text ''PEOPLE MAKE GLASGOW'' can be found on these trash bins in Glasgow. The buildings in Glasgow are also made of red sandstone and yellow sandstone.

cards.a: United Kingdom - Greater Manchester bus stop sign
cards.note:
This busstop sign can be found in Greater Manchester, it has the phone code on it and the M logo on the top left corner with a bunch of other things like a bee on the right. The logo's and phone code can only be seen on one side.

NOTE: A different version can be seen in older coverage, which will be completely white with a huge M logo on it.

Street signs in Leeds District will always have ''LS'' with a number written on the right side. This one is easy to remember because LS stands for Leed-S. The street sign in the top left is only found in the center.

Liverpool street signs often an L on the bottom right corner, standing for Liverpool, towards the centre in the city you will get signs with a unique shape and often have the text ''City of Liverpool'' written on them.
London street signs have a distinct look. They usually feature the street name in black, followed by the postcode and borough in red.
